name: The paper rider that would not settle
subject: practical_science
brief: During the acoustics practical in the physics room, you strike a 256-hertz tuning fork and press its stem to the wooden soundbox of a sonometer. At a bridge span of 32 centimetres the V-shaped paper rider jumps off on one trial, then sits motionless on the next two trials at the same 32-centimetre mark. The digital stroboscope is shared across all six benches.

causes.name: A rust kink on the steel wire near the 32-centimetre mark damps the antinode
The brass end-pulley sticks on its un-oiled pin, so the slotted hanger weight does not tension the wire evenly
The movable knife-edge wooden bridge rocks in a split groove
The tuning fork has a hairline fatigue crack at the base of one prong

tests.name: Sight along the steel wire and watch whether the brass pulley turns when the hanger is nudged
Press the movable wooden bridge and gently lift and release the slotted weight hanger
Gauge wire diameter with a screw gauge and measure bridge squareness with a set-square
Measure wire tension horizontal to the bridge before and after tapping the brass pulley
Repeat the trial with the matched 256-hertz fork from the front cupboard

note: Set in the physics laboratory at Nabapara Vidyalaya (loc_nhss). Resonance should return at the same length every time at constant tension. A brass end pulley that binds on its un-oiled pin leaves a different tension after each adjustment, so the resonant length wanders. A spring balance on the wire, read before and after tapping the pulley, shows the tension jump.
